settings.heading: HireSieve
settings.lede: Drop a folder of CVs in, press one button, and get an evidence-based shortlist where every number quotes the line of the CV it came from. An LLM extracts facts. Python does all the arithmetic. Nothing auto-rejects.
settings.metric: About 45 seconds and a few cents per CV, with the cost shown before it spends

settings.label: Folder in, shortlist out
settings.value: Copy the CVs into the folder for that store and job, press Scan folders, and every candidate is read and ranked against the advert. Inbox intake takes applications from any job board.

settings.label: Evidence per criterion
settings.value: Every score quotes the line of the CV it came from. You can check any number against the document in one click, and a reviewer can see why two candidates rank the way they do.

settings.label: Deterministic scoring
settings.value: The model returns facts and quotes. The scoring engine does every calculation, and it is the only place a number is created — so the same CV against the same advert scores the same every time.

settings.label: Asks before it spends
settings.value: It always shows the count, the folder, the job advert and the cost before sending anything. Over 80 CVs in one run, it asks a second time. Bring your own AI key if you prefer.

settings.label: Roles, pipeline, audit
settings.value: Owner, admin, member and viewer roles; teammates join by invite. Pipeline stages with SLA rules, a provider change audit log, and a multi-location folder tree for high-volume hiring.

settings.label: Undo, retention, documentation
settings.value: Nothing is deleted by mistake: undo removes an assessment, the CV stays, and every batch can be undone. A 12-month retention sweep runs in one command. DPIA, legitimate-interests assessment, ROPA and candidate notices ship with it.

settings.heading: CV screening that keeps a human deciding.
settings.lede: Recruitment screening software for hiring teams with more applicants than hours. Built so the shortlist can be defended line by line.

settings.label: Reject anyone automatically
settings.value: A failed requirement is a label a person can overrule, not a deletion. The full score and the full record are kept either way.

settings.label: Guess whether a CV was written by AI
settings.value: Detectors misfire on about 61% of non-native English writers and show demographic bias. Using one would be a discrimination claim with the claimant's evidence already published.

settings.label: Score spelling, grammar, or which school someone went to
settings.value: Class and race proxies that look like merit.

settings.label: Score a career gap
settings.value: Gaps are shown to a human, never counted against anyone.

settings.label: Produce a number the model invented
settings.value: The model returns facts and quotes. The engine does every calculation, and it is the only place a number is created.

settings.heading: What it deliberately will not do.
settings.lede: This matters more than the feature list, and it is enforced by tests rather than by good intentions.
